file_title: Revolutionary War Pension and Bounty Land Warrant Application File W. 2311, John Wood, Md.
text_original:
Declaration for Bounty Land, by a Widow, under the act of Congress, of March 3d, 1855.
STATE OF Illinois - COUNTY OF Edwards } Set.
On this Eleventh day of April 1855, personally appeared before me, a Justice of the Peace within and for the County and State aforesaid, Rachel Wood
aged Seventy years, a resident of the county of Edwards and State of Illinois - who being duly sworn according to law, declares that she is the widow of John Wood deceased, who was an Ensign in the company commanded by Captain Philip Smith in the regiment commanded by Colonel Johnson of the Maryland Line 1777 -
and performed six months service in the revolutionary war, He was also a Sergeant as Ensign in Capt. Jacob Collins' Company, Catoctie Battalion of Maryland Militia; in the war of the revolution in August 1781 - was also an Ensign in Capt. Wm. McCormack's Compy. Col. James Johnson's Regt. Maryland Militia in 1779 - He was a revolutionary Pensioner under act of March 18, 1818, at $56:66:25 per annum - and was paid at the Pension agency at Springfield, Illinois - No. of application 7729 from Illinois - that her said husband volunteered or enlisted at Frederick County, Maryland, on or about the
day of 1779, for several terms and continued in actual service in the said war for the term of four years, and was honorably discharged at Maryland - on the day of 1781 -
She also drew a pension as his widow under the act of February 3, 1853, for $56:66:25 Certificate of Pension issued August 6, 1853, - application filed from Illinois, April or May 1853. See these Declarations.
She further states, that she was married to the said John Wood in the county of Edwards, and State of Illinois, on or about the 7th day of February, A. D. 1824, by one James Pool who was a Minister of the Gospel; and that her name before her said marriage was Rachel Bratten; that her said husband died in the county of Wabash and State of Illinois, on or about the 11th or 14th day of November, A. D. 1832; and that she is now a widow
She makes this declaration for the purpose of obtaining the Bounty Land to which she is entitled under the act of Congress approved March 3, 1855; and declares that she has never received a Land Warrant on account of the services of her said husband under this or any other act of Congress.
But applied for & received a land warrant No 34478 under the act of Sept 27, 1850 as widow of Daniel Bratten deceased, & +
And finally she hereby constitutes and appoints Richard M. Yotso, of Washington City, her attorney to prosecute her said claim to bounty land, and to receive her warrant therefor, when ready for delivery. John Woods No. of application for a Pension was 7729 - and Rachel Wood as his widow 1751 or 1192 - Both paid at Springfield - Illinois. + see application on file in Pension Office.
Rachel Wood mark
Two witnesses - Attest: a. b. c. d.

text_original:
The State of Alabama, Orphans' Court of Madison County, this 24th day of April 1837 being a day of a Term of the said Court begun and held at the court house in the Town of Huntsville, on the same Monday in said Court (April) 1837.
This day personally appeared in open Court before the Judge thereof, Rebecca McNeely, who represents herself to be the widow of David McNeely, late of said County, deceased, who was in his life-time a Revolutionary Veteran of the United States, as appears by a Certificate of Pension, now here produced by the said Rebecca McNeely, having said at the War Office of the United States, the Thirteenth day of June one thousand eight hundred and thirty. Then appeared, and signed by John Rott, acting Secretary of War, mattering the said David McNeely to receive thirty dollars and twenty five cents per annum during his natural life, the said David McNeely having been a private in the Army of the Revolution, and it appearing to the satisfaction of the Court upon proof made that the said Rebecca McNeely is the widow of the identical David McNeely, deceased, who is named in said Certificate and that the said David McNeely departed this life in said County on the nineteenth day of July eight hundred and thirty six, the same is added to be in the minutes of said Court &c.
I, Richard B. Pindon, Clerk of the County Court of Madison County in the State of Alabama do hereby certify that the above and foregoing is a true copy and complete transcript of the proceedings this day had in the Orphans' Court of said County (which is a Court of Record) touching the application of Rebecca McNeely, widow of David McNeely, deceased, for the amount of the pension due on the Pension Certificate of the said David McNeely, deceased, and which said Pension Certificate is hereto attached.
In Testimony whereof, I hereunto subscribe my name and affix the seal of said County Court, at Office, in Huntsville, this the twenty fourth day of April, A.D. 1837, one thousand eight hundred and thirty seven and of our American Independence the sixty-first.
Richard B. Pindon, Clerk of the County Court of Madison County, Alabama.
FINAL PAYMENT VOUCHER
Received from GAO

file_title: Revolutionary War Pension and Bounty Land Warrant Application File W. 9514, for John Taylor, Maryland
text_original:
Amherst June 7. 1858 To The Commissioner of Pensions
Sir
Application was made and a pension obtained for Seggy Taylor of Amherst County in MD under a power of Attorney from her to myself. She was the widow of a deceased private in the Army of our Revolution and married subsequent to the first of January 1800. A certificate of pension granted to her by the Secretary of the Interior was dated the 32 d day of June 1853 at the rate of twenty five Dollars per annum and by his Construction of the law to take effect from the third day of February 1853 proof of which will be found on file in the Department. The pensioner has since died but left two children.
I have seen by the press that a law has been enacted by the present Congress declaring that the payments of pensions granted under the Act of 1853 shall begin on the 4 th of March 1848 and this letter is written respectfully to inquire whether any additional proceedings are necessary and if so what to obtain the arrears of pension due to Seggy Taylor from March 1848 to Feb 1853. also if agreeable to the rules of your Department would request the favor of a copy of said Act, and have the honor to be very respectfully yr Obedt Servt
Thm Lill Claude

text_original:
Mill Bend Jan. 2. June 1856
Sir:
answered June 6. 1856
Patsy Tucker, widow of Archibald Tucker, who died in service in the war 1812, was pensioned under the half pay act of 16 April 1816. She received a Certificate from the Paymaster Genl's office and was paid for five years at the Nashville Pen. agency. I respectfully enquire If the widow though now married is not by subsequent laws, entitled to additional pension, and if the same is not recoverable by her children, if the same accrued while she remained a widow.
And I further respectfully enquire and ask you to inform me, If the being (now married) will alienate her right to land bounty which might accrue to her in the event of her again becoming a widow under the act of March 1855, Can her and the soldiers children obtain the bounty promised to soldiers dying in the service . If so be pleased to direct me under what law to proceed.
On the 26 ult. I addressed a letter to your office in relation to a Certificate of pension due to Mary Jewell, widow of William in which I intimated that a mistake had been made in the amount allowed . I am fully satisfied that William Jewell of Hawkins County was paid 80 $ per annum at Jonesboro. Pen. and was the husband of Mary the widow in question. There was a William Jewell pensioned under the same law in Davidson County Pen. whose pay may have been different, and whose name may have given rise to the mistake. The Certificate issued to Mary Jewell's admr herewith alluded to date 14 May 1856, allows only 20 $ p. annum. and I respectfully ask a reexamination of the record. as I have said I will withhold the Certificate I have until further advice from your office.
With Very great respect I am your Obedient humble Servant.
A Colonel. L. Burrough Mill Bend Tenn
Honorable J. Minton.
Commr. of Pensions Washington
D.C.

text_original:
Concord N.H. Aug 5 1857
Sir,
Your favor of the 2 d inst in relation to the increase of the pension of Rachel Minor widow of Charles Minor,
I am so strongly of opinion that there is a mistake in your decision that I have ventured to ask that you will consider the case further.
Charles Minor's name is on the Roll of the Agency at the rate of $60 per annum - he was placed on the Pension list Dec. 3 1832 he was a private & served in the Con Militia. It appears that he was paid at the above rate until 1840 when he died. He is inscribed on the Roll of pensioners under the Act of June 7 1832.
From other sources I have the best information that the above statements are correct.
Very Respectfully Yours Obedient L. D. Stevens
Hon E. G. Heath Court of Pensions Washington

file_title: Revolutionary War Pension and Bounty Land Warrant Application File W. 2003, for John Rice, North Carolina
text_original:
Lynchburg, Va Jan 30 1866 Hon. J N Barrett Comr of Pensions
Sir I received the "Restoration" of Pension, No 883 issued to Phebe Rice widow of John Rice, a Lieutenant in Revolutionary war. This certificate states that she is inscribed on the Pension List, at the rate of $240 per annum, commencing on the 4th of March, 1861 and ending August 15, 1861."
I have had nothing to do with prosecuting claims for many years, and I presented this claim at the suggestion of the Provost Marshal of Lynchburg and I do not know that I can presume to question those who manage these things, but if I have the right to do so, I would like to know in the first place, why it is that Mrs Rice is not allowed from 4th day of September, 1860, when she last drew? The Government owes her from 4th of September, 1860, if they owe her from March, 1861, as she never drew it. Is she not entitled to it? If she is, it is my duty to proceed properly to make it. Please inform me.
Then the second certificate No 883, makes the certificate of Pension commencing on the 26th day of December, 1865, and continues for life. There is an interregnum from the 15th of August, 1861 to 26th of December, 1865, making four years, which does not allow any Pension to Mrs. Rice.
Please inform me, if Mrs. Rice is not entitled to this, or at least give me the law or decision which deprives her of it.
Yours ob't Serv't
Chas S. Statham

file_title: Revolutionary War Pension and Bounty Land Warrant Application File W. 5,193, for Leonard Toops, Pennsylvania
text_original:
Harrisburg May 23 d - 1843
James M. Porter Esq r Secretary of War
Dear Sir
Last evening, I received your certificate of Pension to Mrs Margaret Toops, the widow of a Revolutionary pensioner, in conformity with the act of July 7. 1838 allowing her Eighty eight dollars per annum from 4 th March 1836 to 14 th March 1841 — now as this granted to her u by virtue of the Law of Congress, Approved July 7 th 1838 — which Law entitled her to receive the same pension annually, which was allowed to her husband, and as she received a pension of ninety six dollars per annum, why is she allowed but eighty eight dollars per annum? — I knew the old man well from my boyhood, and that he received a pension for near 20 years, and that during the last years of his life. I assisted him in procuring his pension, from the Pension Office in Philadelphia, all which makes me positive of the amount rec d — I have also, the receipts for money paid over — on reference to his account in your department, it will be found to be the major sum: Should this have arisen from an oversight, or mistake, I feel confident you will have justice done to this old lady — you will find on reference to her application made in 1840 testified before you as President Judge of this district, abundant evidence of service rendered by her husband to the U.S. during the Revolutionary War, and of her right to claim also, as his Widow will you please give this your attention, and forward an answer as soon as your business will admit, for if your pension department, have just reasons, for their action, it will suffice, and we proceed immediately to procure the boon of the Government due to this old lady
most respectfully
Your fellow Citizen
John C. Duchay

Sworn to & Subscribed before me on the day & year aforesaid
A Fulkerson J.P.
Chloe Alexander mark

A Fulkerson J.P.

file_title: Revolutionary War Pension and Bounty Land Warrant Application File W. 9340, Hezekiah Baily, Conn. Continental
text_original:
State of Connecticut
County of Fairfield ss
On this 7 th day of June A.D. One thousand eight hundred and fifty five, personally appeared before me a justice of the peace within and for the county and state aforesaid Adah Bailey aged fifty five years a resident of Sa-Saifield in the county and state aforesaid, who being duly sworn according to law, declares that she is the widow of Hezekiah Bailey who was an Ensign & Lieutenant in the revolutionary war and continued in actual service in said war, for the term of fourteen days, and more, and was honorably discharged, and was the identical Hezekiah Bailey who was a pensioner of the United States for said service, at the time of his death, in the sum of five hundred and fifty five dollars and four cents per annum, payable at the pension agency of the United States at Hartford Connecticut, and she states that she does not remember in what company or regiment the said Hezekiah Bailey served, and she says that the proof of the services of the said Hezekiah Bailey was duly made and entered on file in the Pension Department at the time of his application for his open mentioned pension. She further states that she was married to the same identical Hezekiah Bailey at Sa-Saifield open mentioned on the 23 rd day of November A.D. 1833 by one B.G. Morse and that her name before said marriage was Adah Dush, and that she knows of no public record of said marriage. That her said husband died at Danbury in said County and state open mentioned on the 29 th day of January A.D. 1847 and that she has not again married, and is now a widow.
She further declares that she is now a pensioner of the United States, and is the identical Adah Bailey named in an original certificate of Pension now in her possession, of which I certify the following is a true copy -
Department of the Interior
Medal's Pension
I certify that in conformity with the 2 d section of the act of February 3. 1833. Adah Bailey, widow of Hezekiah Bailey, who was an Ensign & Lieutenant in the revolutionary war, is inscribed on the pension list at the rate of five hundred and fifty five dollars, and four cents per annum, commencing on the 3 rd of February, 1833, and continuing for life unless she should again marry, in which case the Pension is not payable after the time of such marriage. Given at the Department of the Interior this twenty second day of June one thousand eight hundred and
examined and countersigned J. P. Kirtland
Commissioner of Pensions
55th House - P. M. Mitchell
Secretary of the Interior

text_original:
Lancaster 25 th October 1839
James L. Edwards Esqr.
Sir.
The Attorney in fact for Mrs. Elizabeth Bausman, widow of William Bausman late a Lieutenant and Torpedo Master in the Service of the United States deceased, and to whom a Certificate of Pension was granted by the Department of War on the 28 th day of September last, for $240. per annum under the Act of Congress of 7 th July 1838 recently presented himself with the Power of Attorney duly authenticated to the Commissioner of Pensions at Philadelphia & was informed by him, that by order of the Department, he was directed to make no payments on any pension certificates bearing date since the 3 rd September last - until after the 1 st March next. As the pensioner in this case, is in very needy circumstances with a large family of daughters whose only support is gained by the precarious employment of their needles. I have contrived to my settled determination, never to be troublesome to you & in consideration of my intimate knowledge of the distress of the old lady in question - at her request, consented to ask, whether or not a special order might not be made directing the payment of the amount due on her Certificate, and forwarded to the Pension Agent at Philadelphia. Your attention to this will much oblige
Yours respectfully
George Rod

Frances Butler

State of Virginia                      SS County of Middlesex
On this 21 st day of March 1855 personally appeared before me a justice of the peace in the county and state aforesaid Elizabeth Clarke aged 84 years, a resident of Middlesex County in the state of Virginia who being duly sworn according to law declares that she is the widow of Spencer Clarke deceased who was a soldier and private in the war of the Revolution - That she is inscribed on the pension list at the rate of ninety six dollars per annum as per certificate now in her possession bearing date on the 14 th day of August 1853 That she has never intermarried since the death of the Spencer Clarke but remains his widow - for proof of marriage & she refers to the papers heretofore filed by her upon the said Certificate of pension was issued - She makes this declaration for the purpose of obtaining the bounty land to which she may be entitled under the act passed the 3 rd day of March 1855. She also declares that she has never received or applied for bounty land under this or any former act of Congress -
Elizabeth x Clarke (seal)
Personally came Mary Mercer and E. J. Mark Clarke residents of the County of Middlesex in the state aforesaid who upon oath declare that they are personally well acquainted with Mrs. Elizabeth Clarke and saw her make her mark to the foregoing declaration that they know her to be the identical person therein represented, and that she is now a widow, and that we have no interest in this claim: Mary x Mercer (seal) E. J. Mark x Clarke (seal)
Elizabeth x Clarke (seal)
The foregoing declaration and affidavit were sworn to and subscribed before me this 21 st day of March 1855, and I certify that I believe the claimant to be the identical person she represents herself to be, that I know the witnesses are credible persons and I have no interest in this claim Rev. L. Garland J. P.

Director of Pensions.
Washington, D.C.
Dear Sir:
In 1845, Josiah Walton, administrator of Priscilla Cotton, widow of Captain Thomas Cotton , renewed the application for pension, under Act of Congress of the 7 th of June 1832, and the 4 th of July 1836, through A. Ferguson as agent. A certificate of pension was issued to Josiah Walton at the rate of $200 per annum from March 4, 1831 to November 18, 1843, the date of the death of Priscilla Cotton (the widow applied for Pension June 29, 1840, shortly before her death in '43.) On Sept. 11, 1851, a certificate for $3,500.00 was received by the estate from the Pension Fund.
Do any of your records give any information as to the birth-place and ancestry of this Captain Thomas Cotton, who served in the Revolution, from North Carolina?
Yours truly,
John T. Cotton

On this 2 nd day of May 1855 personally appeared before the Ambrose P. Hill a justice of the court court of Giles County, in the state of Virginia, aged 78 years, who being first duly sworn according to law doth in her oath, make the following declaration in order to obtain the benefits of the provision made by the act of Congress, passed on the 2 nd February 1848 granting pensions to widows of persons who served during the revolutionary war. That she is the widow of Zachariah Griffin dec d who was "a private and sergeant in the army of the Revolution" and who was a pensioner of the United States, during his life, at the rate of twenty three dollars and thirty two cents per annum, under an act of Congress passed the 7 th of June 1832, which appears by his certificate of pension which issued from the the office of the War Department on the 17 th day of May 1833 signed by Lewis Leaf, Secretary of War, and countersigned by J. L. Edwards Commissioner of Pensions and on the back of said certificate is endorsed "Recorded in the Pension office, in Book E. Vol. 6 page 9", to which certificate, & declaration of her said husband and the evidence accompanying, she begs leave to refer. She further declares that she was married to the said Zachariah Griffin on the 26 th day of January in the year Seventeen hundred and ninety two, that her husband, the aforesaid Zachariah Griffin, died on the 22 nd day of May 1852; that she was not married to him prior to his leaving the service, but the marriage took place previous to the first of January Seventeen hundred and ninety four viz: at the time above stated.

text_original:
Hon'd Sir-
Bushville, Illinois, July 3 d 1843—
Inclosed you will find the declaration of Anna Hinman who is entitled to a renewal of Pension under act of 3 d March 1843 widow of Benjamin Hinman, who was a Deputy Dr. Martin in the Reoly war; a duplicate of which application, was forwarded by mail directed to the Secretary of War or Court of Pensions in March or April last, from which no information has been received—
If the former application was rec'd in your office, I beg leave to call the attention of the department to the letter accompanying it, and if not; to the facts: That Mrs Hinman believes that she was not allowed by her certificate of Pension, dated 12 March 1839, all that she was not entitled to under act, 7 July 1838. her certifi- -cate was filled at 230 Dollars per annum, when it should have been for a larger sum ranging from 240 to 600 $ per annum. as her husband was in the service exceeding 2 years and in the Staff of Major Generals & not Brigadiers, consequently his rank much higher than to be confined to the sum of 230 Dollars —
What is required by the Department & what evidence will be neces- -ary to obtain an increase, we do not know: and if any thing further than the Records at Washington should be required, we should like to be advised. The certificate under the renewal, under the or advice how the pension under the act of 3 d March is to be ac- -quired, will be thankfully rec'd at as early a day as "convenient to the Department; The fact that Mrs H. resides far from Washington City, her application should take precedence in the action of the Department, to those that reside near, where the mails are more expeditious & sure—
respectfully Yours
Hon: J. L. Edwards—
Court of Pensions —
W m A Hinman

text_original:
I Elipha Hatchkiss, of Derby, now aged 60 years, testify, and say, that I am the eldest son, of Levi Hatchkiss late of Derby Connecticut, who was an Ensign, and a Lieutenant, in the Continental Army, in the war of the Revolution. and I well remember that my Father, received a Certificate of Pension in the Spring of the year 1819, entitling him to receive, two Hundred and forty Dollars per annum, to commence, in the month of March 1818. which he received, once, or twice, when his pension was stopped, but for what cause, my Father, never knew. and I further testify that the widow Susannah Hatchkiss, for whom, Mrs Anna French prepared an informal application for a pension, is the widow of my Father, the aforesaid Levi Hatchkiss, and that she is now, and has been, for the last five years past, in the pitiful condition, which her sister, Mrs French, has justly portrayed, — my Father died in Derby, County of New Haven and State of Connecticut. where I now reside, on the 11th day of September A.D. 1831. aged 77 years. In testimony whereof, I have hereunto set my hand, and made oath to the same at Derby aforesaid, this 19th day of October 1837. Before William Storer, a Notary Public. &c, in presence of the subscribing witness, who were knowing to the facts above stated — Elipha Hatchkiss.
Sarah Hatchkiss } Phoebe Phelps } State of Connecticut. County of New Haven. ss. Derby. }
Be It Known, that on this 19th day of October, 1837. before me, William Storer, a Notary Public, within and for the State of Connecticut. and in presence of the subscribing witness, personally appeared, Elipha Hatchkiss, signer of the foregoing disposition, a person known to me, as a man of truth, and veracity, and made oath, to the truth of the above, by him subscribed. —
In testimony whereof, I have hereunto affixed my official signature and seal, the day and year last above written.
